correctness.rationale: Graphical coupling at all vertices: no hub-copy event in a window of duration T, a shared hub fair reset in its first half, and every leaf updating in its second half guarantee identical full configurations at time 0. Independent clocks give probability at most T+(n+1)exp(-theta*T/2), for all n and theta. The decoupled hub has fair resets and produces an independent-leaf Bernoulli mixture driven by a 2-state filtered telegraph. Explicit Beta(a,a) joint densities satisfy both PDMP flux and switching balance with a=theta/[2(1+theta)]; positive reset rates yield its unique invariant law. Conditional binomial characteristic functions converge uniformly as theta grows, producing the arcsine–Gaussian convolution for theta/sqrt(n) finite and its boundary regimes. The majority rule is a continuity event; Gaussian conditional integration and a strictly negative derivative prove the success curve. Standalone exact generator and beta-mixture checks: 680 rational finite-state assertions and 100 additional checks; finite tests do not prove infinite claims.

originality.rationale: Cox–Peres–Steif (arXiv:1408.5122, Section 4) already gives the star Markov reduction and fixed-noise mixing, Caligiuri–Galla (arXiv:2305.19096, Section III.3) gives general two-state PDMP invariant integration, and Carro–Toral–San Miguel (arXiv:1602.06935, Section 2.2) gives general linear network pair-moment equations. Those components are explicitly not claimed new. The accepted claim is a quantitative full-configuration TV comparison between the original interacting star and an independent-hub beta-binomial mixture across diverging noise, and its simultaneous theta~sqrt(n) arcsine-Gaussian majority crossover. The inspected works provide neither the graphical coalescence bound nor a dominating joint-size/noise limit. Targeted published-research and accessible-prior research records comparisons did not find an implication-equivalent result; general high-noise couplings and uninspected full texts remain real historical risks.

value.rationale: The sharp square-root interplay between independent leaf sampling noise and persistent hub-history randomness is a natural inference-scale question on the most degree-heterogeneous connected network. A full-configuration, explicit TV surrogate provides a reusable probabilistic representation; the limiting arcsine–Gaussian convolution and strictly decreasing majority-success curve quantify when the present hub can be inferred above chance at diverging noise. This is more than a bare moment identity or a routine relabeling, and limitations on the sufficient logarithmic separation and Bayes optimality are stated.
